To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of adolescents in Switzerland use social media, but that the use is decreasing.

(a) the majority of the adolescents in the present study are active on social media; (b) adolescents who are more active in social media are more likely to experience social overload; (c) the majority of Swiss adolescents do not experience social media overload and (d) social media overload is related to negative consequences.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
digital media is not only changing childhood, but is also changing the way we think about childhood.
the media is not the cause of all the problems that are associated with children and teenagers, but it is a contributing factor.
digital technologies have the potential to enhance the quality of children's lives and learning, but that this potential is not always realized in practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the digital divide is still very much alive in the lives of adolescents, but that it is not a simple matter of access or lack thereof.
we have been able to demonstrate that there is no single digital divide, but a number of digital divides, which vary by the technology in question and the social group being considered.
we have found that there is a lot of room for improvement in the way that we as a society are dealing with children's use of media and communication technology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the digital world has changed childhoods in many ways, and these changes are often subtle and not always negative.
parents and teachers need to be aware of the potential for cyberbullying and should be proactive in educating their children about how to deal with it.
we need to pay attention to how the media we use to communicate with our families and friends can influence our relationships.
